title: Money and the Heart
subtitle: What the heart does with treasure — four essays, a study, and a book.
forWhom: For the worried and the comfortable alike — the reader who suspects their bank statement is a truer confession than their doctrine.

movements.heading: Read these first
movements.note: Begin with what Jesus actually said, then follow the money past the personal budget to the poor at the gate.

items.label: What the Bible Actually Says About Money
items.blurb: More than two thousand verses, and almost none of them flatter us.

items.label: What Jesus Said About Worry and Money
items.blurb: You cannot serve God and mammon. He said it as a warning, not a paradox.

items.label: What the Jubilee Means
items.blurb: An economy God built to reset every fifty years, and why we quietly filed it under metaphor.

items.label: The Poor Are Not a Ministry Category — They Are the Test of the Church
items.blurb: Scripture does not treat the poor as a program. It treats them as the exam.

movements.heading: Then work the study
movements.note: Where Your Treasure Is is a five-session study on greed, contentment, debt, and generosity — the freedom Christ offers the worried and the wealthy at the same table.

items.label: Where Your Treasure Is — a study on money
items.blurb: Five sessions on what the heart does with what it has.

movements.heading: Then read the book, free
movements.note: On Money & Stewardship gathers the long-form work — debt, generosity, tithing, contentment, and what Jesus meant by mammon. The full book, free.

items.label: On Money & Stewardship — read free
items.blurb: Sixteen chapters on treasure and the heart. Free to read in full.

items.label: Find James's books in the bookstore
items.blurb: Print and ebook editions of the full library.
